source_node_id.description: The node this link leaves, in the earlier stage.

target_node_id.description: The node it reaches, in the next stage.

trace_count.description: How many traces are assigned to both ends.

source_share.description: That count as a fraction of the source node's traces, between 0 and 1.

target_share.description: That count as a fraction of the target node's traces, between 0 and 1. The two shares differ whenever the nodes are different sizes, and reading only one of them is how a thin ribbon gets mistaken for a weak relationship.

ThemeFlow.description: One snapshot read across two to four aspects at once: a stage per aspect, and the links between neighbouring stages. Association, never causation.

snapshot.description: The snapshot this flow was computed from, so every count on the page can be read against the window it came from.

stages.description: One stage per aspect, in the order they were asked for.

links.description: The links between neighbouring stages. There are none between stages that are not neighbours, which is why the order of the aspects matters.

ThemeDetail.description: One theme in one snapshot, or the answer that this snapshot did not hold it.

snapshot.description: The snapshot that was read, with its own counts, so a caller can write `28 of 70 traces in this window` without a second request.

theme.description: The theme, when this snapshot holds it. Absent is an answer and not an error: the theme did not exist in that window, which is what scrubbing a timeline back past a theme's birth looks like. A theme id this entity has never had is a 404 instead.

ThemeExample.description: One note from a theme, with the run it was written about. The two ids are different things: `note_id` identifies the sentence and `trace_id` identifies the run it describes.

trace_id.description: The trace the note was written about.

text.description: The sentence, after redaction. This is the wording that put the trace in this theme, so a reader can see why it landed here rather than take it on trust.

similarity.description: How much this note's wording overlaps the theme's label, counted out of 64. It is a count of shared sketch positions and not a percentage, and it is an integer on purpose: no part of the clustering uses floating-point arithmetic, so two replicas cannot order the same notes differently.

trace_started_at.description: When the run began, so examples can be read against the period they came from rather than against when the note was written.

ThemeExampleListResponse.description: A page of the notes behind one theme.

examples.description: The notes, most like the theme's label first.

ThemeHistoryPoint.description: One theme in one snapshot of its life. Every count belongs to that snapshot alone, and windows overlap, so a run of these is read as a series and never added up.

snapshot_id.description: The snapshot this point comes from.

cutoff_at.description: When that snapshot became the current state.

window_from.description: Start of that snapshot's window, inclusive.

window_to.description: End of that snapshot's window, exclusive.

state.description: What had happened to the theme by this point.

note_count.description: How many notes were in the theme here.

trace_count.description: How many distinct traces those notes were written about.

coverage.description: The theme's share of the notes that snapshot read for this aspect, between 0 and 1. Coverage and raw count can move in opposite directions, and coverage is the one that says whether a theme is gaining ground.

split_from.description: The themes this one came out of at this point. Empty unless `state` is `split`.

split_into.description: The themes that came out of this one at this point. Both directions are stored, so a caller never has to read a second theme's history to learn what happened to this one.

merged_from.description: The themes that became this one at this point. Empty unless `state` is `merge`.

merged_into.description: The theme this one became at this point, when it stopped being its own theme.

ThemeHistory.description: One theme across every stored snapshot that holds it, oldest first. This is the only theme response that names no single snapshot, because the series is the answer.

theme_id.description: The theme this history is of.

aspect.description: The aspect it was clustered along.

label.description: The theme's label at its newest point. A label can change between snapshots, because the note most like the others can change while the theme holds together.

points.description: The series, oldest first, so nothing has to be reordered before it is drawn or differenced.

TraceAspectNotes.description: Every aspect note recorded about one trace, which is at most one per aspect. Read it beside the trace itself: a note is the sentence that put this run in each of its themes, so it is the shortest route from a theme back to what actually happened.

trace_id.description: The trace these notes are about.

notes.description: The notes, in catalogue order. Empty when nothing has written one yet, which is ordinary for a recent trace.

AccountCredentials.description: An email address and a password, for sign-up and for log-in.

email.description: The account's email address. Compared without regard to case, and with surrounding spaces removed.

password.description: At least 10 characters and at most 1024 bytes. Stored only as an argon2id hash.

totp_code.description: The six-digit code from an authenticator app, or one of the recovery codes, when the account has two-step log-in on. Ignored by sign-up.

AccountSession.description: A logged-in session. Send `token` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

token.description: The session token. It is shown once: the daemon keeps only its SHA-256 digest.

expires_at.description: When the session stops working. Log in again after this.

email.description: The account's email address, as stored.

project.description: The project reads go to when they name none. The account's own project, or the first project of the organisation a single sign-on session is limited to. Absent when the session reaches no project yet.

org_id.description: Set when the session came from an organisation's single sign-on. The session then reaches that organisation's projects only.

Account.description: The account a session belongs to.

email.description: The account's email address, as stored.

project.description: The project created with the account at sign-up. Absent for an account that was invited, or created by single sign-on or SCIM.

email_verified.description: Whether the address has been confirmed by a link sent to it.

has_password.description: Whether the account can log in with a password. False for an account created by single sign-on or SCIM that has never set one.

managed_by.description: The organisation that created this account through single sign-on or SCIM. That organisation can deactivate it.

AccountKey.description: One API key an account holds. The secret is not part of it: the daemon keeps only a digest.

id.description: The key's identifier, for revoking it. Not a secret.

project.description: The one project the key reaches.

name.description: The label given when the key was created.

prefix.description: The first characters of the secret, so you can tell which key a process holds without the daemon storing the secret.

created_by.description: The email of the account that created the key. Set in an organisation's key list, so an admin can see whose key it is.

CreateAccountKeyRequest.description: A request for a new API key.

scope.description: What the key may do. One scope per key.

name.description: A label for the key, such as the service that will hold it. At most 100 characters.

project.description: The project the key reaches. Defaults to the account's own project. Your role on the project must allow the scope.

CreatedAccountKey.description: A new API key, with its secret. This is the only time the secret is shown.

key.description: The key as it is listed from now on.

secret.description: The key itself. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`. Copy it now: the daemon keeps only its SHA-256 digest and cannot show it again.

AccountNotice.description: A plain answer that changes nothing you can read back, such as "check your email".

message.description: What happened, and what to do next.

TokenRequest.description: A one-time token from a link the daemon sent by email.

token.description: The token, as it appears in the link.

PasswordForgotRequest.description: A request for a password reset link.

email.description: The address to send the link to. The answer is the same whether or not an account uses it.

PasswordResetRequest.description: A new password, with the token from a reset link.

token.description: The token from the reset link. It works once, for one hour.

password.description: The new password. At least 10 characters and at most 1024 bytes.

totp_code.description: A code from the authenticator app, or a recovery code, when the account has two-step log-in on. A reset proves the address, not the second factor.

PasswordChangeRequest.description: A new password for the logged-in account.

current_password.description: The password in use now. Required when the account has one.

new_password.description: The new password. At least 10 characters and at most 1024 bytes.

EmailChangeRequest.description: A new email address for the logged-in account.

email.description: The new address. A link is sent to it, and the change happens when the link is opened.

password.description: The account's password. Required when the account has one.

AccountDeleteRequest.description: Confirmation for deleting the logged-in account.

password.description: The account's password. Required when the account has one.

totp_code.description: A code from the authenticator app. Required when two-step log-in is on.

orgs_deleted.description: Organisations that had this account as their only member, deleted with it.

projects_erased.description: Projects whose stored signals and runs were erased, because their organisation was deleted.

SessionInfo.description: One live session of the logged-in account. The token is not part of it.

id.description: The session's identifier, for ending it. Not a secret.

current.description: True for the session this request carries.

org_id.description: The organisation a single sign-on session is limited to.

user_agent.description: The browser or client that started it, as it described itself.

address.description: The client address that started it.

TotpSetup.description: A new authenticator secret, not yet in use. Confirm it with a code to turn two-step log-in on.

secret.description: The secret in base32, for typing into an authenticator app.

otpauth_uri.description: The same secret as an `otpauth://` URI.

qr_svg.description: The URI as a QR code, an SVG document.

TotpCodeRequest.description: A code from an authenticator app.

recovery_codes.description: Ten single-use codes that stand in for the authenticator app. They are shown once: the daemon keeps only their digests.

TotpDisableRequest.description: Confirmation for turning two-step log-in off.

password.description: The account's password. Required when the account has one.

code.description: A code from the authenticator app, or a recovery code.

Org.description: An organisation: the owner of projects, members and single sign-on settings.

name.description: Its display name.

quota_per_minute.description: The most signals all its projects together may store per minute. Absent means no ceiling.

retention_days.description: How long its projects keep data, in days. Absent means forever.

managed_by_config.description: True when the daemon's configuration file declares this organisation. Its single sign-on settings are then read from that file and cannot be changed here.

name.description: Its display name, at most 100 characters.

UpdateOrgRequest.description: Changes to an organisation. A field left out keeps its value.

name.description: A new display name, at most 100 characters.

quota_per_minute.description: A ceiling on signals per minute across all the organisation's projects, at most the daemon's own ceiling. 0 restores the daemon's default. Owner only.

retention_days.description: How long to keep data, in days, at most the daemon's own window. 0 restores the daemon's default. Owner only.

projects_erased.description: Projects whose stored signals and runs were erased.

project.description: The project.

project_roles.description: Roles on single projects that replace the organisation role there.

managed.description: True when this organisation created the account through single sign-on or SCIM.

totp_enabled.description: Whether the member has two-step log-in on.

UpdateMemberRequest.description: A new role for a member.

role.description: The role. Only an owner may grant or remove `owner`, and the last owner cannot be demoted.

SetProjectRoleRequest.description: A role for a member on one project.

project.description: A project the organisation owns.

role.description: The role there. Absent removes the project role, so the organisation role applies again.

OrgInvite.description: An invitation not yet accepted. The token is not part of it.

id.description: The invitation's identifier, for revoking it.

email.description: The address it was sent to.

project_roles.description: Project roles it grants as well.

invited_by.description: The email of the member who sent it. Absent when the configuration file or SCIM sent it.

email.description: Who to invite. The link is sent to this address.

role.description: The role to grant. Only an owner may invite an owner.

project_roles.description: Project roles to grant as well.

InviteLookup.description: What an invitation offers, read with its token before accepting it.

email.description: The address it was sent to. Accepting it joins the account with this address.

account_exists.description: Whether an account with this address exists. If it does, log in as it to accept; if not, accepting creates it.

token.description: The token from the invitation link.

password.description: A password for the new account, when no account uses the invited address. Ignored otherwise.

session.description: A session for the account accepting created. Absent when an existing account accepted with its own session.

project.description: The project name. Random, so nobody can choose one that already holds somebody else's data.

created_at.description: When it was created or attached.

CreateProjectRequest.description: A new project in an organisation.

label.description: A display label, at most 100 characters.

OrgUsage.description: How much an organisation is using, against its ceilings. Counted since the daemon started.

quota_per_minute.description: Its ceiling on signals per minute, when it has one.

admitted_this_minute.description: Signals stored in the current one-minute window.

admitted_total.description: Signals stored since the daemon started.

refused_total.description: Signals refused for the ceiling since the daemon started.

retention_days.description: How long its projects keep data, in days.

SsoConfig.description: An organisation's single sign-on settings. The client secret is not part of it.

issuer.description: The OpenID Connect issuer URL. Absent for GitHub.

client_id.description: The client id registered with the provider.

has_client_secret.description: Whether a client secret is stored.

domains.description: Email domains this organisation claims. Single sign-on creates accounts only for these domains, and "Log in with SSO" finds the organisation by them.

enforced.description: When true, members whose email is in a claimed domain cannot log in with a password.

default_role.description: The role given to a member single sign-on creates, when no group maps to a role. Never `owner`.

groups_claim.description: The ID token claim that lists the member's groups, mapped to roles by the group roles.

redirect_url.description: The redirect URL to register with the provider.

managed_by_config.description: True when these settings come from the configuration file.

PutSsoConfigRequest.description: New single sign-on settings for an organisation.

issuer.description: The OpenID Connect issuer URL, such as `https://accounts.google.com`. Required for `oidc`. Must be `https`.

client_id.description: The client id registered with the provider.

client_secret.description: The client secret. Left out, the stored one is kept.

domains.description: Email domains to claim. You can claim the domain of your own verified address. A domain belongs to one organisation.

enforced.description: Refuse password log-in for members in the claimed domains. Turning it on ends their password sessions.

default_role.description: The role for a member single sign-on creates. `admin`, `member` or `viewer`.

groups_claim.description: The ID token claim that lists groups, such as `groups`.

GroupRole.description: A group from the identity provider, and the role its members get.

group.description: The group name, as single sign-on or SCIM sends it. Compared without regard to case.

ScimTokenInfo.description: Whether an organisation has a SCIM token. The token is not part of it.

prefix.description: The first characters of the token.

base_url.description: The SCIM base URL to give your identity provider.

CreatedScimToken.description: A new SCIM token. This is the only time it is shown, and it replaces any earlier token.

token.description: The bearer token for your identity provider. The daemon keeps only its SHA-256 digest.

base_url.description: The SCIM base URL to give your identity provider.

SsoStartRequest.description: Where to start single sign-on. Give one of the two.

email.description: Your email address. Its domain finds the organisation.

org_id.description: The organisation, when you know it.

SsoStart.description: Where to send the browser for single sign-on.

authorize_url.description: The provider's authorization URL, with state, nonce and the PKCE challenge in it.

binding.description: A secret to keep in this browser and send back with the callback. It ties the callback to the browser that started it, so a link from somebody else cannot log you in as them.

SsoCallbackRequest.description: What the provider sent back to the redirect URL.

binding.description: The binding from the start of the flow.

CreatePromptRequest.description: A new version of a prompt. Posting a body identical to the latest version stores nothing new and returns that version, so a deploy that posts its prompts on every start is a no-op when nothing changed.

name.description: The prompt's name. A new name creates the prompt at version 1.

kind.description: `text` or `chat`. Defaults to `chat` when `messages` is set, otherwise `text`.

config.description: Model settings to store with it.

labels.description: Labels to point at the stored version once it is stored, such as `staging`.

PromptLabelRequest.description: Which version a label should point at.

PromptVersionsResponse.description: Every version of one prompt, newest first.

name.description: The prompt's name.

versions.description: Its versions, newest first, each with the labels that point at it.

CreateScorerDefinitionRequest.description: A new version of a scorer definition. A body identical to the latest version is not stored again.

id.description: The definition's id. A new id creates it at version 1.

kind.description: `judge` or `code`.

description.description: What it measures, in a sentence.

direction.description: Which way is better. Defaults to `higher_is_better`.

builtin.description: For `code`: the code scorer to run.

ScorerDefinitionVersions.description: Every version of one scorer definition, newest first.

CreateEvaluationRuleRequest.description: A new version of a live scoring rule. Posting the same body as the latest version stores nothing new.

id.description: The rule's id: lower-case letters, digits, `-` and `_`, up to 64.

enabled.description: Whether it runs. Defaults to `false`, so a rule is read back and checked before it spends anything.

scorers.description: The scorers to run. At least one.

sample_rate.description: The share of matching runs to score, from 0 to 1. Defaults to 1.

name.description: Only runs whose root step has this name.

kind.description: Only runs whose root step is this kind.

tags.description: Only runs carrying all of these tags.

config.description: Settings for the code scorers that need them.

max_judged_per_minute.description: The most judged scores per minute. Defaults to 30.

TrajectoryStep.description: One action an agent took: a tool call, a model generation or a handoff, in the order they started.

index.description: Its position in the trajectory, from 0.

span_id.description: The span it was read from.

kind.description: What kind of action.

name.description: The tool, model step or agent it names.

start_offset_ms.description: When it started, in milliseconds after the run started.

duration_ms.description: How long it took. Absent while it is still running.

model.description: The model, for a model generation.

input_preview.description: The start of its input as plain text, up to 240 characters.

output_preview.description: The start of its output as plain text, up to 240 characters.

tokens.description: Input and output tokens together, for a model generation.

Trajectory.description: A run read as the sequence of actions its agent took. This is what a trajectory is scored on: which tools were called, in what order, how many steps it took, and whether it ended with an answer.

tool_sequence.description: The names of the tool calls, in order. What `expected_tools` is compared with.

tool_count.description: How many of them were tool calls.

final_output_preview.description: The start of the run's answer, from the root step's output.

goal_reached.description: True when the run ended `ok` with a non-empty answer.

ExperimentScoreRequest.description: Which scorers to run over every run recorded under an experiment.

scorers.description: The scorers, as `POST /v1/api/score` takes them. Empty runs the code scorers that need no settings.

config.description: Settings for the code scorers. `expected` is filled per run from the dataset case the run answered, when the run names one.

dry_run.description: Store nothing; report what would be stored.

ExperimentItemResult.description: One case of an experiment: the run that answered it and how each scorer marked it.

trace_id.description: The run that answered the case.

item_id.description: The dataset case, when the run named one in its `mcpd.dataset_item_id` attribute.

input_preview.description: The start of the run's input.

output_preview.description: The start of the run's answer.

expected.description: The case's expected answer, when it has one.

scores.description: The mean value per scorer for this run, keyed by scorer id.

ScorerSummary.description: One scorer's marks across an experiment.

ExperimentResults.description: An experiment case by case, with a summary per scorer. Two of these joined on `item_id` are the per-case comparison of two versions.

items.description: One row per run recorded under the experiment, oldest first.

runs.description: How many runs are recorded under it.

failed.description: How many of them ended in an error.

CreateReviewItemRequest.description: A run to queue for review.

span_id.description: The step, when it is one step.

UpdateReviewItemRequest.description: A change to a review item. Absent fields keep their value.

assignee.description: The new assignee. An empty string unassigns it.

items.description: The items that matched, newest change first.

pending.description: How many items in the project are still pending, whatever the filter.

DatasetVersion.description: A frozen copy of a dataset's cases. An experiment that names a version runs against exactly those cases, whatever has been added to the dataset since.

note.description: What changed since the version before.

created_by.description: Which key or account froze it.

CreateDatasetVersionRequest.description: Freeze the dataset's current cases as a new version.

note.description: What changed since the version before.

Span.description: One unit of work. Spans are the backbone of mcpd: logs, metrics, scores and feedback all hang off a span or a trace.

trace_id.description: 128-bit trace id, 32 lowercase hex characters. OpenTelemetry-compatible.

span_id.description: 64-bit span id, 16 lowercase hex characters. Unique within the trace.

parent_span_id.description: The parent span within this trace. Absent on the root.

external_parent_span_id.description: A parent from a foreign tracing system that mcpd did not create. Carried for correlation, never used for mcpd's own tree.

name.description: What this operation is called. Keep it low-cardinality: `search_docs`, not `search_docs(query=hello)`.

kind.description: What kind of operation this is.

start_time.description: When the operation began, in UTC with nanosecond precision.

end_time.description: When it finished. Absent while the span is still running.

duration_ns.description: Derived from the timestamps at ingest, stored so the database never has to compute it to sort.

is_root.description: True when this span has no parent inside the trace. Materialised so the trace list never scans children.

is_event.description: True for a point in time rather than a duration. Event spans have no end.

entity_kind.description: The kind of thing that produced this span.

entity_id.description: Stable identifier of the producing entity.

entity_name.description: Display name of the producing entity.

input.description: What went in. For a model call this is the full prompt, and it is the single most valuable field mcpd stores.

output.description: What came out. For a model call this is the completion.

attributes.description: Kind-specific structured detail. See the attribute reference for what each kind carries.

metadata.description: Anything you want to attach. mcpd never interprets this.

usage.description: Token counts, on model and embedding spans.

cost.description: Computed cost, on spans that consumed tokens.

model_parameters.description: How the model was called: the sampling settings the caller chose. Absent on a span that made no model call, and on one whose producer did not record them.

links.description: Causal references to other spans or traces.

tags.description: Free labels for filtering. Only meaningful on a root span, where they label the whole trace.

correlation.description: Which project, environment, session, thread and user this belongs to.

model.description: Model identifier, denormalised out of `attributes` so it can be indexed and grouped.

provider.description: Model provider, denormalised for the same reason.

received_at.description: When mcpd accepted this span. Differs from `start_time` for buffered or replayed data, and is what retention is measured against.

ingest_key.description: Producer-supplied idempotency key. A retried batch with the same key is accepted once.

Trace.description: A whole run, projected from its spans. mcpd materialises this at ingest so the list view is one indexed read rather than an aggregation over every span. One per project and trace id: a trace id crosses service boundaries, so two projects that call each other each hold their own run under it, built from their own spans.

root_span_id.description: The root span, when one has arrived.

name.description: The root span's name.

kind.description: The root span's kind.

status.description: `error` when any span in the trace failed, otherwise the root's status.

end_time.description: Latest end across the trace. Absent while anything is still running.

duration_ns.description: Wall-clock span of the whole trace.

usage.description: Token usage summed across every model span in the trace.

cost.description: Cost summed across the trace. This is the number a bill is reconciled against.

model_count.description: How many model calls the run made.

tool_count.description: How many tool calls the run made.

input_preview.description: The start of the root step's input as plain text, up to 240 characters, for a list column. For a chat input it is the last user message. Filled by the trace list when it is asked with `preview=true`; the full input is on the span.

output_preview.description: The start of the root step's output as plain text, up to 240 characters. Filled by the trace list when it is asked with `preview=true`; the full output is on the span.

correlation.description: Context inherited from the root span.

score_summary.description: Mean score per scorer id, maintained as scores arrive, so the list can sort by quality without a join.

feedback_summary.description: Counts per feedback kind and value.

is_complete.description: True once the root span has ended and no span is still open.

received_at.description: When the first span of this trace arrived.

LogRecord.description: A structured log line, correlated to the span that produced it. Logs are stored beside traces so 'show me the logs for this run' is one query, not a context switch to another tool.

trace_id.description: The trace this line belongs to, when it was emitted inside one.

span_id.description: The span this line belongs to.

fields.description: Structured key/value context. Redacted like any payload.

MetricPoint.description: One numeric observation. mcpd aggregates these into time buckets on read, and keeps raw points only as long as the raw retention class allows.

name.description: Metric name, such as `mcpd.model.duration`.

kind.description: How it aggregates.

labels.description: Dimensions. Passed through the cardinality filter, which rejects unbounded keys.

buckets.description: Histogram bucket boundaries and counts, on histogram points.

trace_id.description: Exemplar link: the trace that produced this observation.

span_id.description: Exemplar link: the span that produced it. This is what turns a spike on a chart into a specific run you can open.

Score.description: A machine evaluation of a span or a trace.

span_id.description: The scored span, when the score is about one step rather than the whole run.

scorer_id.description: Which scorer produced this, such as `answer_relevance`.

scorer_version.description: The scorer's version. A score is only comparable to another score from the same version.

min.description: Lower bound of the scale. Without it, a bare number is not interpretable.

label.description: A categorical result, when the scorer produces one alongside the number.

reason.description: Why. For an LLM judge this is the judge's explanation, and it is what makes a score arguable rather than magic.

score_trace_id.description: The trace of the scoring run itself, so a suspicious score can be debugged like any other run.

cost.description: What producing this score cost. Judged evaluation is not free and mcpd refuses to hide that.

Feedback.description: A human evaluation. Kept distinct from `Score` because the two answer different questions and must never be averaged together.

kind.description: Thumbs, rating, correction, tag or comment.

author_id.description: Who gave it. Hashed by default.

author_kind.description: Whether the author was an end user, a reviewer or an operator.

Project.description: The tenancy boundary. Every signal belongs to exactly one project; retention, redaction, sampling, budgets and access are all configured per project.

project_id.description: Stable identifier, used in API paths and ingest keys.

name.description: Display name.

retention_days.description: How long to keep signals. Absent means the server default.

sampling.description: The sampling policy for this project.

redaction.description: Extra redaction rules, applied on top of the server defaults.

budget.description: Cost budget and what happens when it is exceeded.

Dataset.description: A fixed collection of inputs, with optional expected outputs, that an experiment runs against. Datasets are how a change is proved not to regress.

name.description: Display name.

input.description: What to feed the system under test.

expected.description: The reference answer, when there is one. Absent for open-ended cases judged by a scorer.

metadata.description: Anything else, such as a difficulty label or a source citation.

source_trace_id.description: The production trace this case was captured from, when it was. This is how a bug report becomes a permanent regression test.

Experiment.description: One evaluation run of a system against a dataset. Comparing two experiments is how a change is accepted or rejected.

name.description: Display name.

summary.description: Aggregate score per scorer, with mean, standard deviation and count.

baseline_id.description: The experiment this one is compared against.

error.description: Why it failed, when it did.

metadata.description: The configuration under test: model, prompt version, git sha.

AuditEvent.description: One recorded attempt to read stored payloads, or to delete them. Written by the handlers that hand prompts and completions back out of mcpd, so the question "who read this run" has an answer. The audit log is not trimmed by the retention pass: a log that deleted itself on the same schedule as the data it describes could not say who read the data that has since gone.

principal.description: Which key acted, as a short hex digest of it. The key itself is never written here. `anonymous` when the request carried no key, which is what an unprotected daemon looks like.

subject.description: The end identity a proxy asserted for this request. Always empty in this build. The field exists from the first release so that proxy identity can be added later without a migration.

action.description: What was done, named as the endpoint id: `get_trace`, `list_spans`, `delete_trace`.

project.description: The project the request was made against.

resource.description: The trace or dataset the request named, when it named one.

result.description: Whether authorisation allowed the request or refused it.

Definition.description: A stored definition. Immutable per version: a run pins the version it started against, and that version never changes underneath it.

project.description: Which project owns it.

version.description: Its version. A run started without one pins the highest stored version at that moment.

kind.description: What kind of definition it is.

Run.description: One execution of one definition version. The daemon owns the run between steps: its journal, its deadlines, its waits, its cancel and its trace. Your own process owns everything inside a step.

project.description: Which project owns it.

definition_version.description: Which version. Pinned at start and never re-resolved.

cursor.description: The frontier: where in the graph the run has reached.

input.description: What it was started with, after validation against the definition's `input_schema`.

output.description: What the definition's `output` template rendered when the run reached the end of the graph.

state.description: A JSON object merged shallowly on every `complete` that sends one. Later steps read it through the lease.

error.description: Why it failed, when it did: the failing step's message, or the ceiling it spent.

correlation.description: The context stored at start and copied onto every span the daemon writes for the run, with `run_id` set to this run's id.

trace_id.description: The trace every span of this run belongs to. 32 lowercase hex characters, minted at start.

steps_used.description: How many steps this run has completed. Counted against `max_steps` on the root of the run tree.

max_steps.description: The step ceiling from the definition's `limits`, when it declares one. On a root it bounds the whole tree.

cost_usd.description: What the run's steps have cost so far, priced from the usage workers reported.

max_cost_usd.description: The spend ceiling from `limits`, when declared. A claim refused for a spent ceiling ends the run `failed`.

deadline_at.description: When `limits.run_timeout_ms` passes. Absent when the definition declares no timeout, and once the run has ended.

idempotency_key.description: The key the start request carried, when it carried one. A repost of it within 24 hours returns this run.

root_run_id.description: The root of the run tree, which ceilings are enforced against. Equal to `run_id` on a root.

parent_run_id.description: The run whose `subworkflow` step started this one.

parent_step_key.description: The step in the parent that this run is the body of.

depth.description: How many parents lie between this run and the root. Zero on a root.

ended_at.description: When it reached a terminal status.

StepAttempt.description: One attempt at one step of a run. A run's journal is these rows, append only: a retry is a new row, never a rewrite of the old one.

step_key.description: Which step, with any enclosing branch, item or iteration folded into the key: `refund/issue`, `classify[3]`, `poll[7]/classify`.

attempt.description: Which attempt this is. The fence: a lease for an earlier attempt is refused once a later one exists.

kind.description: What kind of step.

effect.description: What a duplicated body would cost.

input.description: The rendered input handed to the worker, on a claimable step.

output.description: What the worker returned on `complete`, or the event payload on a resumed wait.

error.description: Why it failed, when it did.

usage.description: The token usage the worker reported on `complete`.

cost_usd.description: What the daemon priced that usage at.

span_id.description: The span the daemon opened for this attempt. 16 lowercase hex characters, minted when the row was written. A worker's own spans nest under it.

lease_owner.description: The `worker_id` holding the lease, while one does.

lease_until.description: When the lease lapses without a heartbeat.

started_at.description: When the worker posted `started`. Absent when it never did, which is what the reclaim rule reads.

attempts_left.description: How many attempts the node's retry budget still allows after this one.

ended_at.description: When it reached a terminal status.

RunEvent.description: One row of a run's event log. Written in the transaction that made the change it describes, with `seq` allocated from the run header, so a reader that has seen a row has seen every row below it.

seq.description: Its position in this run's stream, from zero and without gaps. Pass it as `after` to reattach.

kind.description: What happened.

Aspect.description: An axis that traces are described along. An aspect is a definition and not a measurement: it carries the name a note is filed under, the words an operator reads on screen and, where a model writes the sentence, the instruction handed to whatever produces it. Four ship with the daemon as ordinary rows rather than as a list compiled into a client, so there is one source of truth for what exists: goal, what the user wanted; sentiment, the tone they expressed; behaviour, what the agent did about it; and outcome, how the interaction ended. A stored version never changes, so a note recorded a month ago still names the definition it was written against.

project.description: Which project owns it. Aspects are project-scoped, like every other tenancy boundary here.

name.description: The aspect's name, lowercase with underscores, such as `goal` or `refund_reason`. This is what a note is filed under and what every query parameter names.

label.description: The display name, such as `Goal`. Stored rather than derived from the name, so an aspect reads the same in every screen and every language of SDK.

description.description: One line saying what this axis is about, shown beside the label so a reader does not have to infer the axis from its name.

instruction.description: The text handed to whatever writes a note along this aspect, at most 2000 bytes. The daemon stores it and hands it out; what reads it and writes the sentence sits outside the daemon. Absent when `derived` is true, because a derived aspect needs no instruction.

derived.description: Whether the daemon writes this aspect's notes itself, with no model anywhere. `outcome` ships derived, written from the run's status, the step error class, the silent producer flag on the cause report and the divergence watch, so a deployment with nothing configured still fills one aspect and can see the whole pipeline work before a model is wired to anything.

built_in.description: Whether the daemon seeded this aspect. A built-in is a row like any other and can be switched off, but it cannot be deleted, because notes already name it.

enabled.description: Whether notes are written along this aspect in this project. It is configuration and read-only here. Switching an aspect on affects notes recorded afterwards and never rewrites what is stored.

sort_order.description: Where this aspect sits in every list and in the default column order, ascending. Stored, so the order an operator learns is the order they keep.

version.description: This definition's version. Editing an aspect stores a new version rather than changing this one, so analysis already recorded is never rewritten under a reader.

AspectNote.description: One sentence recorded against one trace along one aspect. A note proves one thing: that this sentence was recorded against that trace by the definition named in `aspect`, at the version in `definition_version`. It does not prove the sentence is true. Nothing here is checked against the trace it describes, so a note is evidence of what a definition said and not evidence of what happened, and the trace is what settles the difference. The daemon also keeps a small sketch of the wording, which is what clustering compares, and that sketch is deliberately not a field on this entity: it is a detail of how the pass is stored, a caller can do nothing with it, and publishing it would fix the hashing where it stands today. The text is payload. It passes through the same redactor as every other signal on the way in, retention sweeps it, and erasing a subject erases it.

note_id.description: Unique id of the note. This identifies the sentence and never the run: a note id and a trace id are different things and conflating them is the mistake this separate name exists to prevent.

trace_id.description: The trace this sentence is about.

aspect.description: Which aspect this note is filed under, matching `Aspect.name`.

text.description: The sentence, after redaction. It is the only text the read API returns for a note, and it is what the clustering pass reads.

definition_version.description: The version of the aspect definition this note was written against. Editing a definition mints a new version, so an older note keeps naming what was actually asked for at the time.

model.description: Which model wrote the sentence, when one did. Absent for a derived aspect, where the daemon wrote the note itself.

created_at.description: When the note was recorded. Writing a note lags the trace it describes, sometimes by a long way, so a trace can be visible for hours before it carries one.

correlation.description: Inherited from the trace, so a note is scoped, filtered, retained and erased exactly as its trace is.

ThemeSnapshot.description: One clustering pass over one entity, covering a moving window of notes. A snapshot is what turns a clustering into a series: every theme belongs to exactly one, and every theme query names one. Windows overlap, so counts from two snapshots must never be added together. A trace whose note falls inside three windows is counted once in each of them, and summing the three counts it three times. Compare snapshots or read one; do not sum them. Reads never recompute either: a pass writes a snapshot on its own timer and every read is a lookup of what it wrote, so refreshing a screen shows the same numbers rather than a fresh clustering.

snapshot_id.description: Opaque id, echoed back unchanged. Never build one by hand and never read meaning into its shape.

project.description: Which project this pass covered.

entity_kind.description: The kind of thing this pass covered.

entity_name.description: The name of that thing. An entity is the pair of a kind and a name, which spans already carry, so nothing new is assigned to identify one.

aspects.description: The aspects this pass covered, in catalogue order. An aspect with too few notes when the pass ran is absent, so a missing name means it is still collecting and not that anything failed.

ordinal.description: Where this snapshot falls in the entity's series, counting from one at the oldest snapshot still stored.

cutoff_at.description: When this snapshot became the current state. A timeline is ordered by this and not by the window bounds, because two passes can cover overlapping windows.

window_from.description: Start of the window of notes read, inclusive.

window_to.description: End of the window of notes read, exclusive.

trace_count.description: How many distinct traces the notes read belong to.

note_count.description: How many notes the pass actually read. Every coverage figure in this snapshot is a share of this number and never of the number of notes in the window, which is what makes `capped` worth reading.

capped.description: Whether the pass reached its ceiling of 20,000 notes and clustered the newest of them rather than all of them. True means the window holds more notes than were read, so the denominator of every share here is `note_count` and not the window.

Theme.description: A cluster of aspect notes that share their wording, in one snapshot along one aspect. A theme groups aspect notes that share their wording, which is why mcpd needs no model and no embedding to build one. It does not read the sentences, so two notes that mean the same thing in different words land in separate themes, and a theme's label is the note most like the others rather than a summary written for it. The clustering is a pure function of the notes it reads, with no floating-point arithmetic in the comparison, so two replicas of one deployment reading the same notes write the same themes and cannot disagree about where a boundary falls.

theme_id.description: Opaque id, stable across snapshots, which is what makes a history possible. A theme keeps its id while its wording holds, so the same id in two snapshots is the same theme. Nothing is encoded in the shape of it.

snapshot_id.description: The snapshot this theme belongs to.

aspect.description: Which aspect it was clustered along. Clustering runs once per aspect, so one trace can sit in a different theme in each of them.

entity_kind.description: The kind of entity this theme was built for.

label.description: The theme's label, which is the text of one of its own notes: the note most like the rest of them. Nothing wrote it for the screen, so it reads as one real sentence about one real trace rather than as a description of the group, and it can change between snapshots as the group does.

label_note_id.description: The note the label is taken from.

label_trace_id.description: The trace that note was written about, so a reader can open the run behind the label instead of taking the label's word for it.

state.description: What happened to this theme between the previous snapshot and this one.

note_count.description: How many notes are in this theme.

trace_count.description: How many distinct traces those notes were written about.

coverage.description: This theme's share of the notes the snapshot read for this aspect, between 0 and 1. The denominator is the snapshot's `note_count`, so in a capped snapshot it is a share of what was read.

Prompt.description: One version of a named prompt. A version never changes once stored: a new body is a new version, and labels such as `production` and `staging` point at the version a caller should use. SDKs fetch a prompt by name and label, render it with variables, and link the spans that used it, so a trace shows which version produced an answer.

project.description: Which project owns it.

name.description: The prompt's name, unique within the project. Letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` and `/`, up to 128 characters.

version.description: Its version, from 1, assigned by the daemon in the order versions arrive.

kind.description: Whether the body is one template or a list of messages.

template.description: The template, for a `text` prompt. Variables are written `{{name}}`.

messages.description: The messages, for a `chat` prompt: an array of objects with `role` and `content`, where `content` is a template.

config.description: Model settings stored with the prompt, such as `model` and `temperature`. The daemon stores them and does not read them.

variables.description: Every variable the body names, in order of first use, without duplicates.

labels.description: The labels that point at this version now.

note.description: What changed in this version, written by whoever stored it.

created_by.description: Which key or account stored it.

ScorerDefinition.description: A scorer the project defined: a judge prompt written for this agent, or a code scorer with its settings fixed. Stored as numbered versions; a version never changes. Name it in `scorers` wherever a scorer id is taken, as `id` for the latest version or `id@3` for version 3.

project.description: Which project owns it.

id.description: Its id, unique in the project: lower-case letters, digits and `_`, up to 64. It cannot be the id of a scorer mcpd ships.

version.description: Its version, from 1, assigned by the daemon.

kind.description: Judged by the model, or computed by code.

description.description: What it measures, in a sentence. Shown in the scorer catalogue.

direction.description: Which way is better. Comparisons and live alerts read it.

prompt.description: For a `judge` definition: the criterion the model grades against, such as `The answer cites the refund policy by section number.` The daemon adds the run's input and output and asks for a value from 0 to 1 with a one-sentence reason.

builtin.description: For a `code` definition: the code scorer it runs, such as `keyword_coverage`.

config.description: For a `code` definition: the settings the code scorer runs with.

created_by.description: Which key or account stored it.

EvaluationRule.description: A rule for live scoring: which finished runs to score, with which scorers, and how many of them. The daemon reads finished runs as they arrive and scores the sampled ones in the background, so a quality drop shows up in minutes rather than at the next offline pass. Scores it writes have source `live`.

project.description: Which project it scores.

id.description: Its id, unique in the project.

version.description: Its version, from 1. Each change is a new version.

enabled.description: Whether it runs. A rule is stored disabled unless the request says otherwise.

scorers.description: The scorers to run: shipped ids, criteria from the config file, or stored definitions as `id` or `id@version`.

sample_rate.description: The share of matching runs to score, from 0 to 1. Chosen by a hash of the trace id, so the same run is in or out on every replica and every restart.

name.description: Only runs whose root step has this name.

kind.description: Only runs whose root step is this kind.

tags.description: Only runs carrying all of these tags.

config.description: Settings for the code scorers that need them.

max_judged_per_minute.description: The most judged scores the rule may produce in one minute, across the daemon. Each one is a model call, so this caps what the rule can spend. Runs over it are skipped, not queued.

created_by.description: Which key or account stored it.

ReviewItem.description: A run, or one step of it, queued for a person to review. Queue the runs a low score or a thumbs-down flagged, assign them, and mark each reviewed or dismissed; every change is kept, so the item's history says who decided what and when. Corrections and labels go on the run as feedback.

project.description: Which project.

version.description: How many times it has changed, from 1.

span_id.description: The step to look at, when it is one step.

feedback_id.description: The feedback that put it in the queue, when it was feedback.

get.summary: What has arrived since you last looked
get.description: Refresh a list in place instead of running its query again. Hold the cursor from the last poll, send it back, and get the rows that have arrived since, oldest first. The watermark is a row's arrival time and its id together, because a batch writes every row in it with one timestamp and a watermark that could only say 'after this nanosecond' would either replay the whole batch or skip the rest of it. A row written with an arrival time behind the watermark, which a sender can cause by setting `received_at` itself, is not returned; that is the cost of a watermark and no cursor shape avoids it. Sent with `Accept: text/event-stream`, the same request becomes a live tail: the daemon polls every second and sends each batch that brings rows as one `delta` event carrying this response, with the cursor after it as the event id, so a client that reconnects with that cursor misses nothing. A tail closes after thirty minutes and the client reconnects.

get.description:
The cross-aspect view: one stage per aspect, its nodes, and the links between neighbouring stages. A link's count is the number of traces assigned to both of its ends.

This shows association and not causation. A ribbon between a goal theme and an outcome theme means the two were written about the same runs. It does not mean one caused the other.

The order of `aspects` is meaningful and is not a display preference. Links only ever join neighbouring stages, so goal beside outcome answers a different question from goal beside behaviour, and asking for the same aspects in another order asks another question. Fewer than two aspects is refused by name rather than answered with an empty flow, because one stage has no links in it.

Each stage carries at most one noise node and at most one overflow node. Noise is the notes that joined no theme, and it is not a failure bucket: it is rare requests, wording nothing else matched and patterns that have not recurred yet, so a large noise share means varied traffic or too few notes. Overflow is everything past `theme_limit_per_stage`, folded into one node so the stage totals still add up.
